Just as a real quick synopsis of how Roman political corruption slowly turned into feudalism, using a whole lot of generalizations for the sake of not needing an extensive knowledge to understand it... Rome was founded with all citizens holding land. As it expanded, citizens could go out and buy land. As Rome got into wars further from home, the land that was taken was set aside as ager publicus, basically public land for public use and sale. By law it was not supposed to end up in the hands of a few, but it tended to go that way regardless. There was a lot of political agitation about this, especially towards the end of the republic. The citizens were being forced to go fight long extended wars across the Mediterranean, while their farms went to shit. When they returned home, they were broke, their farms were in ruins, and they basically had to sell it off to the rich and work as tenant farmers.

Over the hundreds of years of the empire, this process varied, but had essentially the same results. The rich could get out of paying taxes, the small holders could not, and the small holders ended up losing their land. With the fall of the empire in the west, these lands didnt suddenly open up. They either continued to be held by the same families, or they were taken over by the various tribes and armies that took them over.

In the end, everyone who wasn't rich ended up losing their lands by hook or crook to their rich new land owners. These land owners, or their replacements, became the feudal lords of medieval europe.
